subject: AURA alert · Fri 13 Nov · Emefiele acquired properties through proxies, EFCC tells court
preheader: Also: Afreximbank acquires stake in D’banj’s CREAM platform · 24 stories, 4 risk alerts

overview.text: The Enforcement and Financial Crimes Commission, in a Nigerian court hearing, alleged that former Central Bank governor Chukwuma Emefiele acquired properties through proxies.
The African Export‑Import Bank, through its vehicle CANEX Creations Incorporated, has acquired an equity stake in CREAM, the AI‑powered creative platform founded by Nigerian singer D’banj.
EFCC secured convictions of a mining firm and two other entities in Kwara following a regulatory probe.

cards.headline: Emefiele acquired properties through proxies, EFCC tells court
cards.what_happened: The Enforcement and Financial Crimes Commission, in a Nigerian court hearing, alleged that former Central Bank governor Chukwuma Emefiele acquired properties through proxies. The claim is part of an ongoing probe into potential misuse of office, raising questions about transparency and legality.
analysis: Why it matters: It highlights the possibility that high‑level public officials use intermediaries to conceal ownership of real‑estate assets, undermining transparency and the rule of law.

cards.headline: Afreximbank acquires stake in D’banj’s CREAM platform
cards.what_happened: The African Export‑Import Bank, through its vehicle CANEX Creations Incorporated, has acquired an equity stake in CREAM, the AI‑powered creative platform founded by Nigerian singer D’banj. The deal, formalised on 6 November 2026, is part of the bank’s $2 billion commitment to Africa’s creative sector and aims to boost commercial value and intellectual‑property retention for creatives.
key_facts: Afreximbank acquired an equity stake in CREAM via its vehicle CANEX Creations Incorporated.
Signing ceremony held on 6 November 2026 at the Wole Soyinka Centre in Lagos.
CREAM was launched in 2016 alongside MTN Nigeria and the Bank of Industry.
CANEX WKND 2026 attracted 17,000 participants and targeted at least $1 billion in capital commitments.
analysis: Why it matters: This investment injects significant capital into Nigeria’s creative industry, enhancing financial infrastructure and support for intellectual‑property retention among creators.

cards.headline: EFCC secures conviction of mining firm, two others in Kwara
cards.what_happened: EFCC secured convictions of a mining firm and two other entities in Kwara following a regulatory probe. The action underscores the Commission's commitment to enforcing mining laws within the state.
key_facts: EFCC secured convictions of a mining firm and two other entities
analysis: Why it matters: The convictions demonstrate EFCC's enforcement of mining regulations, reinforcing compliance in the sector.

cards.headline: EFCC re-arraigns ex-Skye Bank chair Tunde Ayeni on N15.6bn fraud charges
cards.what_happened: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has re-arraigned Tunde Ayeni, a former chairman of Skye Bank, on fraud charges totalling N15.6bn. The re-arraignment concerns alleged fraud linked to a former bank chair, a matter of corporate governance accountability in Nigeria's banking sector.
key_facts: EFCC re-arraigned ex-Skye Bank chair Tunde Ayeni.
analysis: As reported by Premium Times; AURA has not checked court or agency records. An allegation or charge is not a finding of guilt.

cards.headline: UNIJOS appoints first female vice-chancellor, Patricia Lar
cards.what_happened: Patricia Lar has been appointed as the first female vice‑chancellor of UNIJOS, marking a milestone in the university’s leadership.
key_facts: Patricia Lar appointed as first female vice‑chancellor of UNIJOS
analysis: Why it matters: This appointment signals progress in gender representation at the highest levels of Nigerian higher education and may influence the university’s strategic direction.

also.text: The Nigerian Senate has summoned the Nigerian Communications Commission and major telecom operators, including MTN, Airtel, Globacom and T2, over persistent network failures and alleged unjustified airtime deductions.
Cross River State Governor Ben Ayade's predecessor-era opposition figure Imoke has insisted that the award of the Mambilla power project contract to Sunrise was invalid.
ICPC has recovered N5.3 billion from local government accounts and will publish the council books online, enhancing financial transparency.
Lagos State announced plans to extend procurement reforms beyond the tenure of former Governor Sanwo-Olu, signalling a new commitment to transparency in public spending.
The Federal Government sealed an Abuja estate after alleged violations of residents’ rights.
The Nigeria Communications Commission announced a new device registration policy that could raise the retail price of mobile phones, according to an expert warning.
Power tariff reforms in Nigeria are reported to be stalled by weak regulatory oversight and market gaps.
The Federal Government has moved to regulate the scrap metal industry in an effort to curb infrastructure vandalism.
Afreximbank and the Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN) have partnered on a $75 million finance facility aimed at small and medium-sized enterprises and the creative sector.
British International Investment (BII) announced a $7m debt facility to Okra, a mesh-grid technology provider for off-grid communities.
